title: Fault type gave no clear added centroid-delay estimate gain for shallow GCMT Mw 6.0-7.5 events in 2012-2020
abstract: We tested whether two fault-type terms improve later-year centroid-delay estimates after moment, depth and broad location are given. We used a fixed Global CMT catalog and selected shallow events with 6.0 <= Mw < 7.5 in 2004-2020. Each year in 2012-2020 used only earlier years for fitting. The test had 807 events. Adding normal and reverse rake classes gave a pooled squared-error reduction of -0.204%. The conditional 95% two-year block interval was -0.537% to +0.149%. Thus the test gave no clear added gain. A planned Mw 6.5 or larger check raised error by 2.22%. Free-depth, finer-longitude and positive-log checks also gave no clear gain. This is a catalog timing benchmark. It does not show that mechanism has no physical effect on rupture. Revised records, origin-time errors, coarse setting controls, one model form and nine test years limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores, all primary uncertainty draws, a figure and an independent numerical audit support reproduction. External event records are excluded.

display.caption: Error reduction from adding fault type in later-year estimates. Negative values mean higher error. Bars give conditional 95% two-year block intervals. Checks change selection, geography or loss.
